title: Tonkatsu
subtitle: crispy fried pork cutlet
excerpt: Tonkatsu is a thick pork loin cutlet coated in panko breadcrumbs and deep-fried until golden and juicy. It is served with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Tonkatsu was developed in Tokyo in the 1890s as a Japanese adaptation of European cutlets. It became one of Japan's favourite Western-style dishes and now has its own dedicated restaurant category called yoshoku.

recipe.temperatureNote: Oil temperature for frying. Do not let it exceed 180C or the outside will brown before the inside cooks.

glossaryTerms.definition: Japanese-style breadcrumbs with a coarser, flakier texture than Western breadcrumbs. They create a lighter, crispier coating when fried.
A category of Japanese cuisine that adapts Western dishes to Japanese tastes. Tonkatsu, omurice and croquettes are classic examples.

content.text: tradition of Western-influenced Japanese cooking. A thick pork loin is coated in
breadcrumbs and fried at a lower temperature than most cutlets so the meat stays moist. Serves 4.
Rest the cutlet for 3 minutes after frying before slicing. This stops the juices running out when you cut it.

items.prepNote: boneless chops, about 180g each and 2cm thick

content.text: Score the fat edge of each pork chop with a knife every 2cm. This stops the cutlet curling in the oil. Season lightly.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, one with panko. Dredge each chop in flour, then egg, then press firmly into panko on all sides.
Pour oil into a wide frying pan to a depth of 2cm. Heat to 170C. Lower two cutlets in carefully. Fry for 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on a wire rack.
Repeat with remaining cutlets. Rest all cutlets on the rack for 3 minutes before slicing.
Mix soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a small bowl. Slice cutlets crosswise and serve over shredded cabbage with the sauce on the side.

attrs.symptom: Coating is dark but meat is raw inside
attrs.fix: Keep the oil at 170C, not higher. Thicker chops need a lower temperature to cook through without burning.

attrs.cause: Breadcrumbs were not pressed on firmly enough
attrs.fix: Press the panko with your whole hand to compact it onto the egg coating before it goes in the oil.

attrs.symptom: Cutlet curls up in the pan
attrs.cause: The fat edge was not scored
attrs.fix: Score the fat at 2cm intervals before coating. This severs the connective tissue that causes curling.

content.text: Tonkatsu restaurants are a whole category of dining in Japan. Specialist shops fry each cutlet to order and serve it with mountains of shredded cabbage. The dish sits in the yoshoku family alongside omurice and hayashi rice. Home cooks make it on weekends when they want something satisfying. The panko crust is what makes it distinctly Japanese.
